author: Jevans Nyabiage
description:
From online-gambling rings in eSwatini to SIM swapping in Kenya and cybercrime networks in Zambia, a wave of cross-border fraud is drawing African governments and China into closer security cooperation.
China hosted East African security ministers and police chiefs in Lianyungang, Jiangsu province, on September 10 for talks on terrorism, kidnapping, online fraud and other cross-border threats.
China’s public security minister, Wang Xiaohong, said Beijing would strengthen law-enforcement...
title: China and Africa boost law enforcement ties in crackdown on cross-border cybercrime

author: Mark Magnier
description:
Christie’s auctioneer Rupert Banner leans forward with practised showmanship as bidding stalls on a rare Yongzheng bowl near New York’s iconic Rockefeller Centre. He pauses as if willing offers from thin air, scanning dozens of in-person buyers and phone banks connecting with China, London, Texas.
It will be a bad look if the frenzy abates for this delicate peach-decorated bowl highlighted on Christie’s glossy Chinese sale catalogue and online advertising. But bidding soon resumes with a...
title: Chinese art takes long march home from US museums

author: Orange Wang
description:
The US is set to deploy one of its signature anti-ship missile systems to the Japanese island closest to Taiwan, an unprecedented move that comes as tensions in the region between Beijing and Tokyo continue to simmer.
The ground-based US uncrewed missile platform known as the Navy-Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction System (NMESIS) will be deployed on Yonaguni Island in Japan’s Okinawa prefecture during biennial joint exercises this month, according to the regional bureau of the Japanese...
title: US to deploy NMESIS anti-ship system on Japanese island closest to Taiwan for first time

author: William Zheng
description:
Chinese troops have taken part in a mass multinational exercise in Russia featuring new anti-drone and ground robot systems – drills that Russian state media said “applied lessons” from the Ukraine war.
The troops were among more than 47,000 military personnel involved in the Tsentr-2026 – or Centre-2026 – drills in the central western Chelyabinsk region from Monday until Saturday.
The Russian Ministry of Defence said the strategic command-and-staff exercise applied combat lessons from the...
title: Chinese troops line up for Russia’s Tsentr-2026 exercise as military ties tighten

author: Victoria Bela
description:
The botanical societies of the United States and China have signed a plant science cooperation initiative, vowing to strengthen bilateral ties and foster an open scientific community to tackle global issues.
The joint initiative was signed during a Sino-American botany conference last month in Taian, in China’s eastern Shandong province, which brought together hundreds of experts from institutions in both countries.
The conference, held from September 19 to 23, aimed to “further deepen botanical...
title: US, China botanists sign landmark proposal on cooperation, global issues and projects

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
For the first time in a decade, China has returned to the top 100 out of 145 economies in an annual global report assessing gender equality.
China closed 69.9 per cent of its gender gap in 2025, rising to 96th place from 103rd the previous year and increasing 1.3 percentage points, according to the 2026 Global Gender Gap Report published by the World Economic Forum (WEF), an international non-profit organisation based in Switzerland.
It marks the first time China has been ranked in the top 100...
title: China returns to top 100 in gender parity ranking for first time since 2016

author: Holly Chik
description:
When chemical engineer Ahmad Zuhairi Abdullah joined Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) 22 years ago, Western institutions dominated the field, from global research infrastructure and high-impact publications to the greatest breakthroughs.
Two decades later, the centre of gravity has moved eastward, says Zuhairi, now a professor with the USM school of chemical engineering in Penang.
“[Not much was known] about China at that time when I joined the university. I knew that they had quite a number of...
title: Malaysia is building a new research corridor across Asia to meet China’s rise: scientists
